name: Balendra Shah
role: Prime minister of Nepal (since March 2026); mayor of Kathmandu (2022–2026)
summary: Shah emphasizes administrative delivery, anti-corruption reform, market-led development with social protection, and cultural preservation. His national agenda stresses climate justice and international cooperation, while film restrictions, evictions and disputes over institutional checks complicate his reformist record.

sources.title: Full transcript of the address to the 81st UN General Assembly, September 24, 2026
sources.author: Balendra Shah; reproduced by The Kathmandu Post/RSS
sources.usedFor: Complete address: climate action, grant finance, global economic reform and future generations. Official UN PDF was blocked; complete published transcript checked against another transcription.

sources.title: 100 Pillars of Policy Departure for Transformation: RSP manifesto, February 2026 (Nepali, 23 pages)
sources.author: Rastriya Swatantra Party
sources.usedFor: Complete downloaded Nepali program: column OCR and visual checks. Explicitly adopted by Shah; program answers medium confidence.

sources.title: I will implement only tried and tested plans: complete interview, May 5, 2022
sources.author: Balendra Shah, interviewed by Pratik Ghimire; The Annapurna Express
sources.usedFor: His municipal agenda, evidence-based implementation and commitment to cultural heritage.

sources.title: Everything You Need to Know About Balen Shah’s Commitment Paper for Jhapa-5 (2026)
sources.author: Nepal News
sources.usedFor: His explicit pledge to lead implementation of the RSP manifesto; farm price guarantees, language curricula and public progress dashboard.

sources.title: Everything You Need to Know About Balen Government’s 100-Point Governance Reform Agenda, March 29, 2026
sources.author: Nepal News
sources.usedFor: First Cabinet meeting: implementing protest inquiry recommendations, administrative reform and public accountability.

sources.title: Patan High Court tells city to allow Indian films in halls. Balen Shah says no, June 22, 2023
sources.author: Onlinekhabar
sources.usedFor: Film ban and his stated willingness to defy the court and accept punishment; linked Facebook original was inaccessible.

sources.title: Nepal: Balen Government Should Bring Human Rights Reforms, May 1, 2026
sources.author: International Commission of Jurists, Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International
sources.usedFor: Documented eviction campaign and proposed constitutional-council ordinance; the organizations’ own policy recommendations are not Shah’s positions.

sources.title: A New Government in Nepal: What Lies Ahead?, March 17, 2026
sources.author: Amit Ranjan, NUS Institute of South Asian Studies
sources.usedFor: Electoral leadership, program and governing challenges; nationalist symbolism distinguished from a specific territorial-recovery policy.

sources.usedFor: Whole mayoral record: health, schools, sanitation, heritage, displaced street vendors and implementation gaps.

notes: No inferred answers. The full 2026 RSP program was downloaded and read using Nepali OCR and visual checks; program positions are medium, grounded in his explicit commitment to lead implementation, not merely party membership. The complete UN speech and 2022 municipal interview were reviewed. Reported implementation and critiques cover both mayoral and national records through 2026. Do not attribute rights organizations’ recommendations to him. His ritual observance does not establish a religious-state policy. A directly elected executive proposal does not answer our head-of-state election item: Nepal’s prime minister and president are distinct offices. The Greater Nepal map is nationalist symbolism, not sufficient evidence of demanding the recovery of all former territories. Film censorship for national identity does not establish moral-character censorship generally. Eviction of unregistered settlements does not establish abolition of private property. Border policing does not establish a preference for fewer lawful immigrants or terrorism surveillance. Digital service delivery is not evidence for rule by AI. All 490 statements and remaining unknowns reviewed.
